messages:
Noah: FYI I'm opening a focused PR to clarify Dedicated provisioning behavior around autoscale and SLA transitions. Draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/634. Main asks: short terraform+terragrunt examples, tighten SLA language, and add one end-to-end SDK snippet for migrate-live.

Asha: Can you add a concrete example of autoscale policy that shows min/max and burst_behavior? Ops wants copy-paste.

Noah: added this minimal YAML in the PR for review:
```yaml
autoscale_policy:
  min_instances: 2
  max_instances: 20
  scale_window: 60s
  burst_behavior: preserve_reserved_then_shared
```

Ben: nice. Two doc fixes I noticed: a stale cross-link to /dedicated/terminology and an old python SDK path. docs-bot, any link-check output?

docs-bot: Link-check results on branch: 2 broken links:
- /dedicated/terminology -> 404
- /sdk/python/tenants/old-provision -> 404
Suggested fixes: update link to /dedicated/glossary and sdk path to /sdk/python/dedicated/provision.

Noah: fixed and force-pushed. Also added a tiny Terraform snippet for creating a reserved pool and attaching a tenant label: 
```hcl
resource "redwood_reserved_pool" "p" {
  name     = "p"
  capacity = 4
  labels   = { team = "payments" }
}
resource "redwood_tenant" "payments" {
  id               = "payments"
  reserved_pool_id = redwood_reserved_pool.p.id
}
```

Asha: Can you add a short "what happens on fallback" paragraph? Customers misinterpret fallback as an outage.

Noah: added a short blurb: "Fallback path (reserved -> shared -> degraded throughput) is an operational path to keep serving, but only reserved-pool healthy capacity is SLA-backed. Degraded throughput may increase latency; not an SLA outage." Kept it explicit.

Ben: SDK snippet request: can we include a combined python example that provisions, probes, and flips route? Nice to have for customer playbook.

Noah: included a compact python example using the current client shape: 
```python
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key=os.environ["REDWOOD_KEY"])
client.dedicated.provision("payments", {"reserved_pool": "p", "autoscale_policy": {...}})
client.dedicated.probe("payments", duration=300)
```

Tara: I ran a quick staging check on the eviction ordering we've documented. One note: under aggressive preemption windows, tenant pods can transiently run on shared nodes before returning to reserved nodes. I added a small runtime caveat to the doc.

Noah: great, added an explicit annotated bullet list under "Eviction & Fallback" with that caveat and a pointer to runtime behavior.

docs-bot: CI + link-checker are green on latest commit.

Asha: I'll polish the SLA wording (shorter, legal-reviewed phrasing) and add a migration checklist (steps + monitoring checks).

Noah: thanks all. Targeting merge by EOD today after SLA wording update and one quick smoke from Tara. Drop any additional snippets on the PR. :rocket:
